newsitem.title: HONG KONG: NATO important in post-Cold War - UK army chief.
newsitem.headline: NATO important in post-Cold War - UK army chief.

text.p: The Cold War may be over, but the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) remains as important as ever for international security, Britain's chief of the defence staff said on Monday.

"Quite clearly, NATO remains the fundamental security alliance as far as the U.K. is concerned," Field Marshal Sir Peter Inge said in a luncheon speech at the Foreign Correspondents' Club in the British colony Hong Kong.
Security may have increased since the breakup of the Soviet Union and the fall of the Berlin Wall, but there was now less peace, Inge said.
"The need to project military power has become more, not less, important," he said.
Inge said there was also the need to foster relations with Moscow.
"Russia is bound to create waves in Europe and Asia," he said. "They mustn't have the right to veto but at the same time we have to be sensitive to Russia's relationship with NATO."

Moscow's opposition to NATO plans to expand eastwards by taking in former members of the defunct Warsaw Pact is expected to dominate the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) summit, which opened in Lisbon on Monday.
The 54-nation OSCE encompasses all European nations along with Canada and the United States.
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told the summit that Moscow firmly opposed NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

The 16-nation NATO's immediate tasks, Inge said, included the political and military challenges of adding new members, changing the command structure and developing the Partnership for Peace programme.
The programme, launched in 1994, is designed to bring together nations split along former Cold War frontiers.
It now groups 27 countries in central and eastern Europe and all the former Soviet republics except Tajikistan as well as neutral Finland, Austria, Sweden and Switzerland.
Britain was also taking steps to improve military ties with China, said Inge, who met People's Liberation Army (PLA) Chief of General Staff Fu Quanyou last week in Beijing.
"My sense is that they are very keen, as we are very keen, to improve the relationship," he said. China resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong at midnight next June 30.
